doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Supper clubs close in the 1960s and the venues that replaced them
summary: As supper clubs faded she played the Copley Plaza, Village Gate, Village Vanguard, Mikell's and Jimmy Weston's.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: In the 1960’s, many of the supper clubs that you had been playing in began to close. How did that affect your career?
Well, I would cry but everything doesn’t last forever. Life doesn’t last forever. So you have to wait ‘til the time comes back.

Supper clubs are something that as a rule, don’t exist today like they did. Are there any other places that opened up as a result—are there any other sectors of the entertainment economy, or venues, that started booking the kinds of acts that the supper clubs used to?
The Copley Plaza, places like that. And the Village Vangate [Village Gate], the Village Vanguard. Some of the clubs on the West Side, Mikell’s Pub, Jimmy Weston’s.
When did you start playing some of those others, Jimmy Weston’s for example?
